title: Inverse image, tensor product and extension by zero preserve $D^b_c(-,\mathcal O_E)$
statement:
Let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite and all schemes Noetherian.

1. For $f\colon X\to Y$ and $K\in\Dbc(Y,\cO_E)$, $f^*K\in\Dbc(X,\cO_E)$.
2. For $K,M\in\Dbc(X,\cO_E)$, $K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\cO_{E,X}}M\in\Dbc(X,\cO_E)$ (no completion is
   needed).
3. For a locally closed immersion $a=i\circ u\colon S\hookrightarrow\overline S\hookrightarrow X$
   and $L\in\Dbc(S,\cO_E)$, $a_!L=i_*u_!L\in\Dbc(X,\cO_E)$.
4. For $a$ as in (3), $L\in D(S_{\mathrm{proét}},\cO_E)$ and $M\in D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\cO_E)$,
   $(a_!L)\otimes^{\mathbf L}M\simeq a_!(L\otimes^{\mathbf L}a^*M)$.

proof.text: Use the integral coefficient ring sheaf $R_T=\mathcal O_{E,T}$ and write $A=\mathcal O_E$. Here $\Dbc(T,A)$ means bounded complexes with constructible cohomology, with finite constant local models $R_V\otimes_A P$ for finitely presented scalar $A$-modules $P$, as in [sk-def-sfb-constructible, sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]. Thus we can prove membership directly from cohomology and strata; we do not assume that an arbitrary bounded complex of finite free modules splits into its terms. No additional completeness condition is inserted into this definition.

source.place: opening paragraph, interpreted using the current definitions

proof.text: For clause (1), [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients] identifies $f^*R_Y=R_X$ and says that module pullback is exact inverse image. It therefore preserves kernels, images, cokernels and cohomology, so $H^q(f^*K)=f^*H^q(K)$ with the same bounds. For each constructible $H^q(K)$ pull its finite stratification back to $X$ using [lemma-constructible-pullback-stratification]. Pull each pro-étale covering of a stratum back to its fibre product with $X$; it is again a covering: weakly étale arrows remain weakly étale by [lem-weil-pbc-weakly-etale-composition-base-change], and the family remains fpqc by [lem-galois-fpqc-covering-base-change]. The covering definition [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] then applies, even though the new base is not an object of the old small site. A scalar finite presentation $A^m\to A^n\to P\to0$ gives $R_V^m\to R_V^n\to R_V\otimes_A P\to0$; exact inverse image pulls this cokernel presentation back to the same scalar matrix over the new coefficient ring. Thus the pulled-back cohomology has finite constant local models. The pulled-back strata are locally closed and hence constructible on the Noetherian scheme $X$. This proves $f^*K\in\Dbc(X,A)$ for every $f$, without any finite-type or field-base hypothesis.

source.place: paragraph (1): exact inverse image and pullback of strata and covers

proof.text: For clause (3), first take an open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow T$ and its complementary closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$. Every open subset of a Noetherian topological space is quasi-compact, by Noetherian induction on closed subsets: if a finite subcover did not exist, choose a minimal closed subset on which it fails; removing one cover member containing a point gives a proper closed subset, covered finitely by minimality, and adjoining that member contradicts minimality. Apply this standard lemma to the underlying Noetherian spaces; the open immersion is quasi-compact. With the inverse-image coefficient rings, [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] says that $j_!$ and $i_*$ are exact, restrict to the identity on their own loci, and restrict to zero on the complementary loci. The coefficient rings agree with $R_U,R_Z$ by [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients]. Given a finite stratification for a constructible sheaf on $U$ (respectively $Z$), regard its strata as locally closed subschemes of $T$ and append the complementary closed (respectively open) locus. On the original strata the extended sheaf has the same scalar local models; on the added locus its model is zero. Hence both functors preserve constructible sheaves. Since they are exact, their termwise functors commute with cohomology and preserve bounds, proving preservation of $\Dbc$. Apply the open conclusion to $u:S\hookrightarrow\overline S$ and then the closed conclusion to $i:\overline S\hookrightarrow X$ to obtain $a_!L=i_*u_!L\in\Dbc(X,A)$.

For the tensor calculation first take constructible sheaves $F,G$ in degree zero. Intersect their finite stratifications, forming the actual fibre products of strata using [lemma-constructible-pullback-stratification]; the intersections are locally closed, disjoint and cover $X$. On each stratum $T$ intersect the two pro-étale trivializing covers by fibre products $V_\alpha\times_T W_\beta$. The base-change and composition axioms of a site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] make this a covering: first pull the second cover back over each member of the first, then compose. On its objects $V$, exact inverse image and the scalar cokernel argument of step 2 identify the two sheaves with $R_V\otimes_A P$ and $R_V\otimes_A Q$ for finitely presented scalar modules $P,Q$. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], the restriction of $F\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{R_X}G$ is the derived tensor of these two models.

proof.text: The ring $A=\mathcal O_E$ is a DVR, and each nonzero element is a unit times a power of a uniformizer $\pi$ [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr]. Choose a finite free surjection $A^n\twoheadrightarrow P$, with kernel $N\subset A^n$. By [lem-sc-dvr-saturation-line-smith-normal-form] the inclusion of $N$ has a diagonal matrix in finite bases, of rank at most $n$. Each diagonal entry is nonzero because the inclusion is injective, and can be replaced by $\pi^r$ after multiplying a basis vector by a unit. Taking the cokernel gives a finite direct sum decomposition of $P$ into copies of $A$ and $A/\pi^r$ with $r\geq1$; unit entries give zero summands. Do the same for $Q$. Right exactness of ordinary tensor gives decompositions of the two local models into copies of $R=R_V$ and $R/\pi^rR$.

source.place: tensor paragraph: expand the finite free local calculation using scalar Smith normal form

proof.text: The constant-to-completed coefficient map $A_V\to R_V$ is flat by clause (1) of [det-prop-integral-criterion-constant-coefficients]. The constant presheaf map given by multiplication $A\xrightarrow{\pi^r}A$ is injective because $A$ is a domain. Its sheafification is multiplication on the constant ring sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] and is still injective by exact sheafification [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact]. Flatness here means that the sheaf tensor functor $-\otimes_{A_V}R_V$ is exact [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Applying that functor to the kernel sequence $0\to A_V\xrightarrow{\pi^r}A_V$, and identifying $A_V\otimes_{A_V}R_V=R_V$, gives the kernel sequence $0\to R_V\xrightarrow{\pi^r}R_V$. Hence this multiplication on $R$ is injective. Consequently $[R\xrightarrow{\pi^r}R]$, placed in degrees $-1,0$, resolves $R/\pi^rR$. It is K-flat directly from [def-pc-kflat-complex]: tensoring it with any acyclic complex gives the cone of multiplication by $\pi^r$ on that complex, up to the usual shift, which is acyclic by the cohomology long exact sequence [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact]. Also $R[0]$ is K-flat because tensoring with it is the identity. Thus these explicit complexes compute the derived tensors, using [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom].

proof.text:
Tensoring a free summand with another summand leaves it in degree zero. For two torsion summands the explicit resolution of step 6 gives
$$ (R/\pi^rR)\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}(R/\pi^sR)\simeq[R/\pi^sR\xrightarrow{\pi^r}R/\pi^sR]. $$
If $r\geq s$, the differential is zero, so both cohomology sheaves are $R/\pi^sR$. If $r<s$, the cokernel is $R/\pi^rR$ and the kernel is $\pi^{s-r}R/\pi^sR\cong R/\pi^rR$. To check the latter for sheaves, lift a quotient section locally to $x\in R$. The equation $\pi^r x=0$ modulo $\pi^s$ means, after a refinement, $\pi^r x=\pi^s y$. Cancellation using step 6 gives $x=\pi^{s-r}y$. For the map $R\to R/\pi^sR$, $y\mapsto\pi^{s-r}y$, a section in its kernel locally satisfies $\pi^{s-r}y=\pi^s z$. Injectivity of $\pi^{s-r}$ gives $y=\pi^r z$; conversely every $y=\pi^r z$ maps to zero. Its kernel is therefore exactly $\pi^rR$. Thus in both cases $H^{-1}$ and $H^0$ are $R/\pi^{\min(r,s)}R$, and other cohomology vanishes. Finite sums give the calculation for the local models in step 5. These resulting cohomology sheaves have finite constant scalar models, and all local tensors have amplitude in $[-1,0]$. Exact restrictions commute with cohomology. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-stratum-detection], these restrictions detect vanishing outside that interval globally. The models themselves give constructibility by [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Hence $F\otimes^{\mathbf L}G\in\Dbc(X,A)$.

proof.text:
Extend the sheaf calculation to clause (2) by two finite cohomological inductions. The standard truncation triangles of [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category] give, for bounded $K$ with cohomology in $[a,b]$,
$$\tau_{\leq b-1}K\longrightarrow K\longrightarrow H^b(K)[-b]\longrightarrow(\tau_{\leq b-1}K)[1].$$
Derived tensor is exact in each variable [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact], and $\Dbc(X,A)$ is a triangulated subcategory on Noetherian $X$ [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]. Fix a constructible sheaf $G$. The empty interval is the zero case and the one-degree case is step 7 shifted. Tensoring the displayed triangle with $G$, the first term is handled by induction on $b-a$ and the third by the sheaf case; closure under triangles gives $K\otimes^{\mathbf L}G$. Now fix such a $K$ and induct on an interval $[c,d]$ containing the cohomology of $M$. The empty interval is again zero, the one-degree case is the conclusion just established shifted, and the triangle for $M$ gives outer terms $K\otimes^{\mathbf L}\tau_{\leq d-1}M$ and $(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}H^d(M))[-d]$. They belong to $\Dbc$ by induction and the first induction. Therefore the middle term $K\otimes^{\mathbf L}M$ belongs to $\Dbc$. All these are ambient derived tensors; no completion is taken.

proof.text:
For clause (4), prove the open projection formula on the unbounded ambient categories. For $j:U\hookrightarrow T$, the pro-étale site of $U$ is the localized site of $T$ at $U$ [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization], and the coefficient ring restricts to $R_U$ [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients]. Choose a representative complex for $L$ and a K-flat resolution $P\to M$ with flat terms [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. The complex $j^*P$ is K-flat with flat terms by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Thus $j_!L\otimes^{\mathbf L}M$ is represented by $j_!L\otimes P$, and $L\otimes^{\mathbf L}j^*M$ by $L\otimes j^*P$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-extension-tensor] in each bidegree. Since $j_!$ is left adjoint to $j^*$ and exact [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed], it preserves the direct sums in totalization [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits] and induces its termwise derived functor. Write the bidegree isomorphism as $\theta_{p,q}:(j_!L^p)\otimes P^q\to j_!(L^p\otimes j^*P^q)$. Naturality in its first argument makes $\theta$ commute with the maps induced by $d_L^p$, and naturality in its second argument makes it commute with the maps induced by $d_P^q$. Additivity then makes it commute with their signed sum $d_L\otimes1+(-1)^p1\otimes d_P$ in bidegree $(p,q)$. Summing these maps over $p+q=n$ gives an isomorphism of total complexes, naturally
$$j_!L\otimes^{\mathbf L}M\simeq j_!(L\otimes^{\mathbf L}j^*M).$$
This argument imposes no bounds or constructibility on $L,M$.

proof.text:
For a closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ with open complement $j$, $i_*$ is exact since $T$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed]. Thus $Ri_*=i_*$ termwise and $Li^*=i^*$ because the coefficient system is Cartesian [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients]. The natural projection map of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] is
$$i_*N\otimes^{\mathbf L}M\longrightarrow i_*(N\otimes^{\mathbf L}i^*M).$$
Its restriction by $i^*$ is the identity on $N\otimes^{\mathbf L}i^*M$: the defining mate uses the counit $i^*i_*N\to N$, which is an isomorphism, and the monoidal pullback comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Its restriction by $j^*$ is a map $0\to0$, since $j^*i_*=0$ and pullback commutes with derived tensor. The identities and vanishings are those of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed]. The two strata $Z,U$ jointly detect isomorphisms by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-stratum-detection], so this projection map is an isomorphism for arbitrary $N,M$.

Finally apply step 10 with $N=u_!L$ and then step 9 inside $\overline S$:
$$ (i_*u_!L)\otimes^{\mathbf L}M\simeq i_*(u_!L\otimes^{\mathbf L}i^*M)\simeq i_*u_!(L\otimes^{\mathbf L}u^*i^*M)=a_!(L\otimes^{\mathbf L}a^*M). $$
Here $a^*=u^*i^*$ by composition of inverse-image functors [lem-weil-pbc-site-morphism-composition] and the Cartesian coefficient identifications already fixed. Both factors are the ambient, exact immersion functors from step 3. This proves clause (4) with precisely its stated arbitrary derived objects and is natural in both arguments.

split_report.summary: All four clauses unchanged. Prove exact functor preservation directly from the current finite constant local model definition; replace the false finite-sum-of-shifts assertion by Smith decomposition, explicit two-term resolutions and two finite truncation inductions. Derive open and closed projection formulas separately on arbitrary unbounded objects. Reuse existing nodes only; avoid the circular integral-model/heart dependencies and finite-type-over-a-field preservation lemmas.
split_report.blueprint: Proof paragraph (1) is step 2; paragraph (3) is step 3; the local tensor and dévissage paragraph (2) is steps 4–8; paragraph (4) is steps 9–11. The preliminary completeness criterion is unnecessary for the current stated definition.

tool_uses.why: Base change of a finite stratification supplies the strata for pullback and common refinement; the integral-model unit has no separate stratification lemma.
Exactness, adjunctions and complementary vanishings of module immersion functors give extension preservation and the closed projection formula; these are general pro-etale topos identities.
The general unbounded monoidal pullback theorem transports each local tensor and preserves the K-flat resolutions needed in the open projection formula.
The scalar valuation ring is a DVR with a uniformizer and unit-times-power decomposition; these scalar facts are not an operation-preservation clause.
Conservativity of finite stratum restrictions detects the tensor cohomology bounds and the closed projection-map isomorphism.
Exactness of derived tensor supports the two finite truncation inductions, and the explicitly defined mate supplies the canonical closed projection map.
The small pro-etale site over an open is the slice site, allowing the general ringed-slice tensor identity to apply.
Unbounded module complexes on a ringed site admit K-flat resolutions with flat terms, used to prove the open projection formula without boundedness assumptions.
The sheaf-level tensor identity for extension from a slice yields the open derived formula bidegree by bidegree; it does not restate the integral constructibility clauses.
Composition of inverse-image functors identifies a^* with u^* i^* when the two immersion formulas are composed.
Exact sheafification carries the injective scalar constant-presheaf map to an injective constant-sheaf map before flat change of coefficients; this is a general site tool.
